title: Unique Viewpoint | Dify.AI’s Zhang Luyu: LLM App Success Hinges on Resources & Market Beyond Tech
summary: On January 24, 2024, Unique Capital and partners held the 2024 AIGC Application Development Summit in Shanghai (~1,000 AI practitioners). Edited from the guest keynote dialogue.
author: Unique Research
html:
Unique Research · Unique Viewpoint · March 25, 2024

Background

On January 24, 2024, Unique Capital and partners held the 2024 AIGC Application Development Summit in Shanghai (~1,000 AI practitioners). Edited from the guest keynote dialogue.

Guests

  • Zhang Luyu — Founder & CEO, Dify.AI
  • Yin Zhi — Chief Advisory Consultant, Shanghai AI Technology Association

Bottlenecks for LLM app landing (IT stack view)

Zhang: Dify is a service-oriented open-source middleware to help enterprises and developers ship LLM apps — covering data and ops pain. Across many builders, the first question he asks is: Who are you? Identity shapes scenarios and failure modes. Models are only part of an app — often <50%; the rest is product DNA, original customers, and accumulated resources. Common pattern: process apps = LLM + orchestration + legacy logic. Others are interaction- or data-centric. SaaS firms with clear user needs have a simpler path; uncertain experiments without understanding model properties tend to fail.

What frameworks will the industry need in 2024?

Zhang: Early half-year was fragmented POC with OpenAI APIs/SDKs or LangChain glue. Paradigms are clarifying around two parts: (1) RAG pipelines — indexing, cleaning, query (kin to prior data mid-platforms); (2) app orchestration — logic + prompts + multi-size commercial/open models into multimodal apps (kin to RPA).

Value of AI dev platforms (incl. Dify) for enterprises

Zhang: Exploration predated OpenAI’s GPT Store / Assistants-style surfaces by ~half a year. Value stack:

  • Near-term: fast, low-cost near-POC prototypes
  • Learning: prompt-first skills for traditional software teams
  • Mid-term: engineering convenience for complex pipelines, multi-source data, multi-model assembly and performance
  • Long-term: post-launch data collection, labeling, feedback to improve prompts and models — no AI app stays static

Yin notes prior “AI Four Dragons”-era full stacks already faced heavy engineering (data import, automation) before RAG/agents — new tools simplify some steps but add new complexity.

Will Dify offer MaaS?

Zhang: No — MaaS (cloud train/infer) fits cloud vendors’ compute/scheduling strengths. Dify focuses on problems after you have a model. Yin expects model choice to converge toward a few OS-like options (iOS/Android analogy).

Ideal one-stop framework — who can build apps?

Zhang: Vision: make AI definable and usable by everyone — developer vs non-developer less binary. GPTs-class tools lower the floor for small experiments; professional/monetized products still need integration, UX, and domain skill. Analogy: small apps as easy as Excel formulas; real products still demand craft.

Platform trends: ToC vs ToB

Zhang: ToC platforms may sit with mega traffic entrances or top model vendors (OpenAI-like standards). Enterprise platforms emphasize private data/security — e.g., agent platforms over internal data + tool APIs. Differentiation also by model size: small models → mobile-like frameworks; large models → internal AI mid-platforms.

Big tech vs startups

Zhang: Startups win on speed and developer focus — Dify’s product (Jun 2023 launch) already >16,000 GitHub stars; BAT/model vendors began copying similar surfaces. “Seat problem”: model vendors optimize for their models; clouds optimize for selling compute. Startups optimize for getting developers’ apps live.

Yin: Large firms have infrastructure flexibility — algorithms must eventually run on domestic hardware (e.g., Huawei stack).

2024: ToC fire or ToB scale?

Zhang: ToC is emergent — unpredictable creativity, hard to SOP; builder population may not massively expand. ToB: same app pattern can replicate across thousands of enterprises — many deployments, fewer categories. Different dynamics, both real.

4 CN images; attach on ingest.

— END —
